Final TraceWin policy benchmark¶

This report focuses on one configuration only: final_thesis_031_a015_s025_steps300k, evaluated on real TraceWin workspace 2 over 20 matched-reset episodes with a maximum of 30 steps.

It contains only the artifacts needed for the final decision:

  • dataset-031 policy training;
  • the exact bar and box plots from this 30-step benchmark;
  • reliability-based selection of the best policy;
  • comparison with warm-started Bayesian Optimization;
  • operational timing at the end.

No training or TraceWin simulation is launched here. The notebook reads the saved artifacts and renders a concise, reproducible summary.

In [1]:

def find_repository_root(start=Path.cwd()):

1. Dataset-031 training¶

All policies were optimized using the dataset-031 surrogate setup. Model-free agents use a budget of 300,000 environment steps over three seeds (42, 43 and 44). SVG differentiates through the surrogate dynamics and therefore does not interact with the environment through the classic step-by-step RL loop. The curves below are surrogate evaluations during training; final selection is based on the real-TraceWin benchmark in section 2.

2. Final evaluation on real TraceWin: 30-step episodes¶

Each promoted policy is evaluated over 20 matched reset seeds on workspace 2. Every episode can run for at most 30 steps and terminates earlier if the beam is lost. A failure is a final score equal to ERROR_SCORE = -999. The ranking uses the final state left by the policy, not the best state visited temporarily during its trajectory.

In [3]:
benchmark_30 = json.loads(BENCHMARK_30_PATH.read_text())
tracewin_30 = benchmark_30["policy_evaluation_tracewin"]
episodes_30 = pd.DataFrame(tracewin_30["episodes"])
error_score = float(benchmark_30["score_function"]["error_score"])


def compact_summary(tracewin, episodes, error_score):
    raw = pd.DataFrame(tracewin["summary"]).T.copy()
    failures = episodes.groupby("algorithm")["final_score"].apply(
        lambda values: int(np.isclose(values, error_score).sum())
    )
    medians = episodes.groupby("algorithm")["final_score"].median()
    result = pd.DataFrame({
        "episodes": raw["episodes"].astype(int),
        "score mean": raw["final_score_mean"],
        "score std": raw["final_score_std"],
        "score median": medians,
        "mean npart ratio": raw["final_npart_ratio_mean"],
        "failures": failures,
        "failure rate": failures / raw["episodes"],
        "best observed score": raw["best_observed_score"],
    })
    return result.sort_values("score mean", ascending=False)


summary_30 = compact_summary(tracewin_30, episodes_30, error_score)
display(summary_30.style.format({
    "score mean": "{:.2f}", "score std": "{:.2f}", "score median": "{:.2f}",
    "mean npart ratio": "{:.3f}", "failure rate": "{:.0%}",
    "best observed score": "{:.2f}",
}).background_gradient(subset=["score mean"], cmap="RdYlGn"))

bar_plot_30 = BENCHMARK_30_DIR / "benchmark_policy_bars_tracewin.png"

The reliable top group is td3, svg_final, sac and svg_uniform: all complete the 20 episodes without losing the beam. TD3 ranks first by final-score mean (58.01 ± 5.55) and also has the largest observed score (66.12). ppo, ddpg and especially a2c are not suitable deployment candidates because terminal failures dominate their averages.

3. Bayesian Optimization reference¶

The reference campaign contains five independent warm-started runs with 300 new real-TraceWin evaluations each. Its best score is a selected static optimum, not a mean across reset episodes, so it is not inserted into the policy ranking. The plots show convergence and the best configuration's shift from the nominal machine settings.

In [4]:

4. Final decision¶

  • TD3 is the policy to test: 58.01 ± 5.55 final score, zero failures and best observed score 66.12.
  • Bayesian Optimization reaches 60.36 as a selected static optimum; this is competitive, but it is a different statistic from a policy's mean across resets.
  • ppo, ddpg and a2c are rejected because of terminal beam-loss risk.

5. Timing: one Bayesian run vs one TD3 test episode¶

This final comparison considers the intended operations after policy selection:

  • one complete Bayesian run: 300 TraceWin evaluations;
  • one TD3 test episode: 30 environment steps, hence 30 TraceWin calls.

Bayesian durations are measured from saved timestamps. The TD3 duration is estimated as 30 × measured mean TraceWin-call time, because the policy benchmark does not record timestamps.

In [5]:
def parse_timestamp(value):
    return datetime.fromisoformat(value)


timing_rows = []
for run in bayesian_report["runs"]:
    timed = [row for row in run["evaluations"] if row.get("timestamp")]
    timestamps = [parse_timestamp(row["timestamp"]) for row in timed]
    duration_seconds = (max(timestamps) - min(timestamps)).total_seconds()
    timing_rows.append({
        "run": int(run["run_index"]) + 1,
        "TraceWin calls": len(timed),
        "duration min": duration_seconds / 60,
        "average s/call": duration_seconds / max(1, len(timed) - 1),
        "best score": run["best_score"],
    })

bayesian_timing = pd.DataFrame(timing_rows).set_index("run")
mean_call_seconds = (bayesian_timing["duration min"].sum() * 60
                     / (bayesian_timing["TraceWin calls"].sum() - len(bayesian_timing)))
mean_bayesian_run_minutes = bayesian_timing["duration min"].mean()
td3_episode_minutes = 30 * mean_call_seconds / 60

display(Markdown("**Measured Bayesian duration by run**"))
display(bayesian_timing.style.format({
    "duration min": "{:.1f}", "average s/call": "{:.1f}", "best score": "{:.2f}",
}))

timing_comparison = pd.DataFrame([
    {"operation": "TD3: one 30-step test episode", "TraceWin calls": 30,
     "duration min": td3_episode_minutes, "basis": "estimated: 30 × mean call time"},
    {"operation": "Bayesian Optimization: one complete run", "TraceWin calls": 300,
     "duration min": mean_bayesian_run_minutes, "basis": "measured mean across 5 runs"},
]).set_index("operation")
display(Markdown("**Direct operational comparison**"))
display(timing_comparison.style.format({"duration min": "{:.1f}"}))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.5, 5.0))
labels = ["TD3\n30 steps", "Bayesian\n300 calls"]
values = [td3_episode_minutes, mean_bayesian_run_minutes]
ax.bar(
    labels,
    values,
    color=["#2A9D8F", "#E9A23B"],
    alpha=0.9,
    width=0.52,
    edgecolor="white",
    linewidth=0.8,
)
for index, value in enumerate(values):
    ax.text(index, value, f"{value:.1f} min", ha="center", va="bottom")
ax.set_title("Elapsed-time comparison", loc="left")
ax.set_ylabel("Minutes")
ax.set_ylim(0, max(values) * 1.12)
ax.grid(axis="y")
ax.grid(False, axis="x")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Direct operational comparison

  TraceWin calls duration min basis
operation      
TD3: one 30-step test episode 30 12.2 estimated: 30 × mean call time
Bayesian Optimization: one complete run 300 121.6 measured mean across 5 runs

A TraceWin call takes 24.4 seconds on average in the recorded Bayesian campaign. Therefore, one TD3 episode is approximately 12.2 minutes, while one complete Bayesian run takes 121.6 minutes on average. The Bayesian run costs about 10 times more calls and wall-clock time than one deployment episode of the already selected policy. Policy training is excluded because it was performed offline on the surrogate.
